polr_action: Enter FFG lifecycle. Qualify homeowner status at Month 1 settlement call. If homeowner=yes, flag FHL cross-sell eligible and begin lifecycle nurture toward Month 6 soft intro and Month 9 Momentum Pack. If homeowner=unknown, add to homeowner qualification queue.
communication_principle: Focus on FFG relationship first. Build trust through lifecycle touchpoints before introducing FHL. No FHL mention until Month 6 at earliest.
example_scenario: Brad settles a $45K car loan for a 35-year-old professional. During Month 1 call, broker confirms they own a home in Footscray. POLR flags FHL cross-sell eligible and queues Month 9 Momentum Pack.

polr_action: Enter FHL lifecycle. Customer is already a homeowner (inherent from FHL). At Month 9, deliver ICA-targeted FFG Momentum Pack. Bill Robb owns the cross-sell conversation. Track engagement with portal and content to refine ICA assignment.
communication_principle: FHL lifecycle is the primary relationship. FFG cross-sell is introduced naturally at Month 9. 'You trust us with your home. Let us look after your car and equipment too.'
example_scenario: Paige settles a $650K refinance. Customer enters FHL lifecycle. At Month 9, POLR delivers FFG Momentum Pack based on ICA 2 (Established Personal Finance). Bill calls to discuss.

polr_action: Run both lifecycles in parallel. Coordinate messaging to avoid overlap (never send FFG and FHL touchpoints in the same week). Prioritise whichever lifecycle has the next cross-sell moment. Engagement score reflects activity across both businesses. Annual review (Month 12) covers full financial picture across both loans.
communication_principle: This is the ideal state — full Fox customer. Communication should reinforce the 'one team for all your finance' message. Avoid treating as two separate customers. Single POLR dashboard showing all products.
example_scenario: Customer has a $55K car loan (FFG, settled 6 months ago) and a $580K home loan (FHL, settled 2 months ago). POLR runs both lifecycles but coordinates: FHL Month 3 Confidence Pack goes first, FFG Month 9 Momentum Pack is adjusted to not overlap.

polr_action: Standard FFG sales pipeline. No cross-sell activity — focus on converting the FFG lead first. Capture homeowner status during qualification if possible (add to intake form or qualification call). Store for future FHL routing post-settlement.
communication_principle: Conversion first. Do not distract with FHL messaging. The goal is to settle this loan. Homeowner data capture is background intelligence, not a conversation topic.
example_scenario: New lead from dealer wants a $28K used car finance. FFG broker qualifies them. During application, broker notes they rent. POLR stores homeowner_status=no. FHL cross-sell becomes long-term FHB nurture post-settlement.

polr_action: Standard FHL sales pipeline. No FFG cross-sell during qualification — focus on converting the home loan. Note any vehicle or equipment needs mentioned during conversation for post-settlement FFG routing.
communication_principle: Conversion first. FHL is a complex, high-value sale. Do not muddy the waters with FFG offers during qualification. Park any FFG signals for post-settlement.
example_scenario: Referral from accountant for $720K investment property purchase. Bill qualifies the lead. Customer mentions needing a new ute for the rental property. Bill notes in POLR but focuses on the home loan.

polr_action: FFG application in progress. No FHL activity. Focus on getting FFG application approved and settled. Homeowner status may become known through application documents (asset/liability statement). If discovered, store in POLR for post-settlement routing.
communication_principle: Application stage is anxious for customers. Keep focus entirely on their FFG application progress. Any FHL signals are stored silently.
example_scenario: Customer has submitted FFG application for $65K equipment. Asset/liability statement shows a property worth $850K with $400K mortgage. POLR stores homeowner_status=yes, property_value=$850K. FHL cross-sell queued for post-settlement.

polr_action: FHL application in progress. No FFG activity. Focus on FHL approval and settlement. Application data enriches POLR profile (income, employment, assets). Store any vehicle/equipment mentions for post-settlement.
communication_principle: Home loan applications are stressful. Keep all communication focused on FHL progress. Do not introduce FFG during this stage.
example_scenario: First home buyer has FHL application submitted for $520K purchase. Application reveals they currently drive a 2015 Corolla. POLR notes potential vehicle upgrade need for post-settlement FFG approach.

polr_action: Cross-sell is already working — this customer was routed from FHL to FFG. Continue FHL lifecycle in parallel. FFG application gets priority processing (existing customer gets VIP treatment). Once FFG settles, both lifecycles run.
communication_principle: Reinforce the 'one team' message. 'We already look after your home loan — getting your car sorted is easy because we already know your situation.' Fast-track where possible.
example_scenario: FHL customer at Month 9 responded to FFG Momentum Pack. Now applying for $55K new vehicle through FFG. Bill handed off to Brad with full FHL context. Application is being processed.

polr_action: Cross-sell is already working — this customer was routed from FFG to FHL. FFG lifecycle continues but pause any FHL-related messaging (they are already in FHL pipeline). FHL application gets warm context from FFG history. Once FHL settles, both lifecycles run.
communication_principle: The customer is already bought in. FFG lifecycle continues (loan servicing) but cross-sell messaging stops — they are already converting. Focus FHL comms on application progress.
example_scenario: FFG customer at Month 9 expressed interest in home loan refinance. Now has FHL application with Bill for $600K refinance. FFG lifecycle continues for car loan servicing but Month 9 Momentum Pack is marked as 'converted'.

polr_action: Cross-sell pipeline active. FFG lifecycle continues. FHL lead status means Bill has been introduced and initial qualification is underway. POLR tracks FHL pipeline progress alongside FFG lifecycle. Coordinate so FFG touchpoints don't compete with FHL qualification calls.
communication_principle: Warm transition. Customer has expressed interest in FHL. Keep FFG lifecycle going but avoid FHL cross-sell messaging (they are already in the FHL pipeline). Let Bill run the FHL qualification without noise.
example_scenario: FFG customer responded to Month 6 soft FHL introduction. Bill has made contact and is qualifying their home loan needs. FFG lifecycle continues but POLR suppresses further FHL cross-sell content.

polr_action: Cross-sell pipeline active in reverse direction. FHL lifecycle continues. FFG lead status means customer has expressed interest in asset finance. Route to FFG broker with full FHL context. FHL lifecycle continues — pause FFG cross-sell messaging (they are already converting).
communication_principle: Customer is responding to FFG Momentum Pack or annual review. FFG broker has context from POLR. Let the FFG conversation run naturally.
example_scenario: FHL customer at Month 9 clicked through FFG Momentum Pack and requested a call. POLR creates FFG lead, routes to Brad with customer's FHL history, ICA profile, and employment details.

polr_action: FFG application was declined. Assess decline reason. If credit-related, check UMI eligibility (with customer consent). Keep in POLR for future re-engagement. Do NOT cross-sell FHL — declined customer is not in a receptive state. Set 6-month re-engagement timer.
communication_principle: Empathy first. They just got bad news. Handle with care using Doc 7 (Declined Application Script). No cross-sell of any kind. The door stays open for when their situation improves.
example_scenario: 22-year-old (ICA 1) declined for $18K car loan due to thin credit. FFG broker uses Doc 7 script. With consent, refers to UMI as alternative. POLR sets 6-month re-engagement flag.

polr_action: Unusual but possible — FHL customer whose FFG application was declined (business structure issue, specific asset issue, etc.). FHL lifecycle continues unaffected. FFG decline reason documented. Do not re-approach for FFG unless circumstances change. Annual review at Month 12 can reassess.
communication_principle: Delicate. Customer trusts Fox with their home loan but was knocked back on asset finance. Acknowledge it professionally. FHL relationship must not be damaged by FFG decline. Do not bring up FFG again until customer initiates or annual review.
example_scenario: FHL customer with $700K mortgage applied for $120K equipment finance but FFG declined due to ABN < 2 years. FHL lifecycle continues. At Month 12 annual review, Bill checks if business has matured enough for FFG re-application.

polr_action: FFG customer whose FHL application was declined (credit, income, LVR issue). FFG lifecycle continues. FHL decline reason documented. Do not re-approach for FHL unless circumstances change materially. Mark fhl_cross_sell_status as paused with review date.
communication_principle: FFG relationship continues normally. FHL decline should not affect FFG service quality. If customer raises it, be empathetic. Set a 12-month review flag — circumstances may change.
example_scenario: FFG customer (ICA 5) was introduced to FHL at Month 9 but application declined due to insufficient deposit (LVR too high). FFG lifecycle continues. POLR sets 12-month FHL review flag.

polr_action: Former FFG customer (loan discharged or closed). Keep in POLR as dormant. Do not actively cross-sell to FHL — relationship has lapsed. Include in re-engagement campaigns (Doc 9 win-back script) at 6 and 12 month intervals. If they re-engage, reassess for both FFG and FHL.
communication_principle: Light touch. They were a customer once. Periodic check-in, not aggressive outreach. 'Just checking in — anything we can help with these days?'
example_scenario: Customer paid out their FFG car loan 8 months ago and has had no contact since. POLR triggers 12-month re-engagement email using Doc 9 win-back approach.

polr_action: Former FHL customer (loan discharged, refinanced elsewhere, or property sold). Keep in POLR as dormant. Include in re-engagement campaigns. If they sold property, they may need new FHL services. If they refinanced elsewhere, understand why (retention failure analysis).
communication_principle: Respectful re-engagement. They left for a reason. Understand why before re-approaching. If they refinanced elsewhere, a humble 'we'd love to earn your business back' approach.
example_scenario: FHL customer refinanced with a competitor 6 months ago. POLR logs reason (better rate offered). At 12 months, Bill sends a market update and offer to review their current position.

polr_action: Former FFG customer who still has an active FHL loan. FHL lifecycle continues normally. FFG re-engagement is natural through FHL lifecycle cross-sell moments (Month 9 Momentum Pack, Month 12 Annual Review). No separate FFG win-back needed — let the FHL lifecycle do the work.
communication_principle: FHL is the active relationship. FFG re-engagement happens organically through lifecycle touchpoints. Don't force it. The Month 9 Momentum Pack is the natural moment.
example_scenario: Customer paid out their FFG car loan 2 years ago. Still has FHL mortgage at Month 15. FHL lifecycle naturally re-introduces FFG through Refinance Pathway content.

polr_action: Active FFG customer who lost their FHL loan (refinanced elsewhere, sold property). FFG lifecycle continues. Investigate FHL loss reason. If sold property — may need new FHL services. If refinanced elsewhere — note competitive loss and flag for future. FFG annual review can probe gently.
communication_principle: FFG relationship continues warmly. FHL loss is noted but not dwelt on. At FFG annual review, a natural check-in: 'How's the property side going? Still happy with your home loan setup?'
example_scenario: Customer has active FFG equipment loan but refinanced their mortgage with a competitor. FFG lifecycle continues. At Month 12 annual review, broker gently explores if FHL can earn them back.

polr_action: Fully lapsed customer. Both relationships ended. Keep in POLR as dormant. Annual re-engagement email only (not aggressive). If they re-enter through any channel, treat as warm lead with full history context.
communication_principle: Minimal contact. Annual check-in at most. They may come back when a new need arises. POLR remembers them so if they do return, it's seamless.
example_scenario: Customer had both FFG car loan and FHL mortgage but both are now closed (car paid off, house sold). POLR sends annual 'we're still here' touchpoint. 18 months later, they call about financing a new car — POLR pulls up full history.

polr_action: PRIMARY cross-sell trigger. Deliver ICA-targeted FHL cross-sell pack via POLR portal and email. Create priority handoff task for Bill Robb. Bill must call within 24 hours. This is the highest-value moment in the FFG lifecycle for FHL conversion.
communication_principle: Month 9 Business Growth Pack / FHL cross-sell moment. Warm, value-led messaging: 'You've been building equity. Here's how Fox can help you make the most of it.' ICA-specific pack ensures relevance.
example_scenario: ICA 3 (Prime Repeat) customer at FFG Month 9. Homeowner confirmed. POLR delivers premium vehicle + home equity pack. Bill calls: 'You've trusted us with your car for 9 months. Let me show you what we can do with your home loan.'

polr_action: Customer is not a homeowner. FHL cross-sell is long-term FHB nurture only. At Month 9, instead of Momentum Pack, deliver FHB education content (savings tips, government grants, deposit strategies). No hard cross-sell. Add to POLR FHB nurture track.
communication_principle: Nurture, not sell. 'Thinking about buying your first home one day? Here's what you need to know.' Plant seeds but no pressure. This could be a 12-24 month journey.
example_scenario: ICA 1 (Young Practical Motor) customer at FFG Month 9. Renter. POLR delivers FHB education pack instead of Momentum Pack. No Bill Robb call — automated content only.

polr_action: CRITICAL DATA GAP. Homeowner status should have been captured by now (Month 1 or Month 6 at latest). Create urgent task for FFG broker to qualify homeowner status before delivering Month 9 content. If qualification fails, send generic Month 9 content without FHL cross-sell.
communication_principle: Cannot cross-sell without knowing homeowner status. The FFG broker must make a call to qualify. Frame as a check-in, not data collection.
example_scenario: FFG customer at Month 9 but homeowner_status=unknown (broker missed it at intake and Month 6). POLR creates urgent task. Broker calls: 'Just checking in on your loan — by the way, are you currently renting or do you own your place?' Answer determines Month 9 content.

polr_action: PRIMARY cross-sell trigger (FHL → FFG direction). Deliver ICA-targeted FFG Momentum Pack. This is the confirmed Month 9 touchpoint from the FHL lifecycle plan. Bill Robb coordinates with FFG broker. 5 ICA variations + equity release pack.
communication_principle: 'You've built equity. Here's how Fox Finance Group can help you make the most of it.' ICA-specific messaging ensures the asset finance offer is relevant to their profile.
example_scenario: FHL customer (ICA 4, Business Asset Borrower) at Month 9. POLR delivers equipment and fleet expansion Momentum Pack. Bill introduces Sam Drew for a business finance conversation.

polr_action: Proactive Pricing Review touchpoint. Bill calls to review rate and negotiate repricing if needed. Light FFG introduction ONLY if customer mentions car, equipment, or business needs during the call. Do not force FFG into the conversation.
communication_principle: This is a value demonstration moment (rate review). FFG is mentioned only if the customer opens the door. 'By the way, if you ever need help with car or equipment finance, we have a team for that too.'
example_scenario: FHL customer at Month 6 Pricing Review. Bill calls, negotiates $800/year rate saving. Customer mentions they need a new work ute. Bill notes in POLR, says 'let me connect you with our asset finance team.' Creates FFG lead.

polr_action: Dual-customer at FHL Annual Review. This is the comprehensive financial picture moment. Review covers both FFG and FHL loans, property valuations, equity position, and life changes. Single meeting covering everything. Referral request. If FFG loan approaching balloon/end-of-term, discuss renewal.
communication_principle: 'Let's look at your full financial picture.' This customer is the dream — they trust Fox with everything. Make them feel valued. One meeting, complete review, no wasted time.
example_scenario: Customer has FFG equipment loan (Month 18, balloon approaching) and FHL mortgage (Month 12 Annual Review). Bill and FFG broker do a joint review. Cover property valuation, equipment refinance options, and referral ask.

polr_action: Prospect only — registered on POLR portal but no active relationship with any business. Trigger needs assessment flow (quiz or questionnaire). Route to appropriate business based on responses. If no engagement after 30 days, move to low-frequency nurture.
communication_principle: Curious, not pushy. 'Welcome to POLR. Tell us what you're looking for and we'll point you in the right direction.' Let the customer self-select.
example_scenario: Someone finds the POLR portal online and registers. Completes needs assessment quiz indicating interest in car finance. POLR creates FFG lead and routes to broker team.

polr_action: Unusual combination. FFG declined but separately enquiring about FHL. Could be different timing or different needs. Treat FHL lead on its own merits. FFG decline history is noted but does not prejudice FHL qualification (different criteria, different products).
communication_principle: FHL assessment is independent. A car finance decline does not mean a home loan decline. Treat the FHL inquiry fresh. If customer raises FFG decline, acknowledge and reassure.
example_scenario: Customer was declined for FFG car finance 4 months ago (credit issue). Now inquiring about FHL refinance (has property, good equity). FHL qualifies them on home loan criteria independently.

polr_action: Customer is simultaneously in both pipelines. Coordinate between FFG broker and Bill Robb. Avoid duplicate outreach. Decide which business takes lead on communication (usually whichever the customer contacted first). Share context between teams via POLR.
communication_principle: 'We can help with both.' Single point of contact where possible. Customer should feel like they're dealing with one company, not two separate businesses chasing them.
example_scenario: Customer calls FFG about car finance and in the same week submits an FHL refinance inquiry online. POLR flags the overlap. Bill and FFG broker coordinate — Bill takes lead since home loan is higher value, bundles the car finance conversation.

polr_action: Both applications in progress simultaneously. Coordinate timelines. Share financial data between applications where permitted (same customer, one profile). If FHL application impacts FFG serviceability or vice versa, flag early. Single status update cadence.
communication_principle: Streamlined experience. 'We're working on both at the same time.' Avoid asking for the same documents twice. One POLR profile, shared data.
example_scenario: Business owner (ICA 4) applying for $200K equipment (FFG) and $900K commercial property (FHL) at the same time. Bill and Sam coordinate. Serviceability assessment covers both applications together.

polr_action: FFG customer settled but homeowner status never captured. This is the #1 data gap. Create qualification task for FFG broker at next touchpoint (Month 3 at latest). Until homeowner_status is known, FHL cross-sell cannot be routed. Block Month 9 Momentum Pack until status confirmed.
communication_principle: Homeowner qualification is a background task. Frame it naturally: 'Just updating your profile — are you currently renting or owning?' Do not make it feel like an interrogation.
example_scenario: FFG customer settled 2 months ago. Homeowner_status=unknown. POLR creates task for Month 3 check-in: broker must ask about housing situation. Until answered, no FHL content is queued.
